newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields up, fear Macfarlane/jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields up, fear Macfarlane/jobs.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed higher as the market braced for two key events on Thursday -- RBA governor Macfarlane's testimony to parliament and the April labour force report.
*Second stage of U.S. refunding later on Wednesday.
Australian bond yields closed higher as the market braced for two key events on Thursday -- Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane's testimony to parliament and the April labour force report.

The spike in yields was triggered by the unwinding of speculative futures trades just after the opening when the central bank left official interest rates at 6.0 percent after Tuesday's board meeting.
This unchanged policy stance had been widely predicted, although the futures fall sparked off further long liquidation in both in physical and futures positions, traders said.

"Genuine (rather than speculative) long positions in cash and futures took the opportunity to liquidate when there was no change in interest rates. People are nervous ahead of Macfarlane and the jobs figures," one trader said.

Macfarlane addresses a parliamentary finance committee on Thursday, the first of his semi-annual testimonies, and his comments will be heavily scanned for the cental bank's current thinking on policy and the general economic outlook.
Around the same time, the April labour report is due to be released and is expected to show a strong rebound in employment after its recent weak performance.

Median forecasts centre on a 35,000 rise in employment, but this is not expected to impact on the unemployment rate, which is seen sticking at 8.7 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
Before then, the U.S. Treasury market faces the second and final stage of the quarterly refunding later on Wednesday with the auction of A$12 billion of 10-year notes.
The U.S. market came slight pressure on Tuesday after a poor response to a three-year note sale, and the reaction to today's auction is expected to set the initial local tone on Thursday.

The local market underperformed against the U.S. and Canada, which also faces a C$2.4 billion 10-year bond sale later on Wedesday. New Zealand bonds were under pressure from a weak N.Z. TWI and after RBNZ governor Brash failed to reassure the market that its recent easing stance was appropriate.
